chunks: Fadala ibn Sinan narrated from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Hakam ibn al-Husayn from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is no ugly action but that I have performed it; is there for me any repentance?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) replied: 'Are any of your parents alive?' He said: 'My father.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Then go and be kind to him.' So when he had left, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commented: 'If only it was his mother!'
ai.seo_question: What is the best way to repent for major sins according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) prescribes serving one's living father as a specific expiation for a man burdened with all manner of sins, illustrating the Shia scholarly view that filial piety (*birr al-walidayn*) holds immense purifying power. The Prophet’s remark, 'Had his mother been alive!', underscores the superior merit of the mother in Islamic ethics, a theme frequently emphasized in Shia hadith literature regarding the hierarchy of parental rights.
